topics.title: Cool Math Magic Trick
topics.text:
Credit: Arthur T. Benjamin



Hey guys! I just found this cool magic trick that will find the day of any date in the years 2000-2031. Here is how it works:



Each month in a year has a code as follows:

Month CodesJanuary: 6

February: 2

March:2

April: 5

May: 0

June: 3

July: 5

August: 1

September: 4

October: 6

November: 2

December: 4




Each year also has a code:

Year Codes2000: 0

2001: 1

2002: 2

2003: 3

2004: 5

2005: 6

2006: 0

2007: 1

2008: 3

2009: 4

2010: 5

2011: 6

2012: 1

2013: 2

2014: 3

2015: 4

2016: 6

2017: 0

2018: 1

2019: 2

2020: 4

2021: 5

2022: 6

2023: 0

2024: 2

2025: 3

2026: 4

2027: 5

2028: 0

2029: 1

2030: 2

2031: 3




Now to actually find the day, we do the following calculation:



Month Code + Date + Year Code (mod 7)



For example, for todays date, August 22, 201, we would preform the following calculation:



$1+22+1 \pmod{7}=24 \pmod{7} = 3.$



The third day of the week is Wednesday, so August 22, 2018 is a Wednesday (which is true). What I am still puzzled about is how we get the numbers of the month codes and the year codes. Any ideas?

topics.title: Manhole covers are round.
topics.text:
I was walking around the streets and wondered about manhole covers. I wondered about their shape. "All manhole covers seem to be circles. I have never seen any cover that's a square or any other shape.". Because of this, I searched it up on the internet for the reason why, and this was the answer:





"Why are manhole covers round, instead of squares?"



"A round manhole cover cannot fall through its circular opening, whereas a square manhole cover could fall in if it were inserted diagonally in the hole."





Now, I became curious. "Are circles the only shapes that work for this? Do there exist another shape which could also work as a manhole cover for the same reason?"
